gen-gf-baumans-gf-arvo: Baumans looks commanding and distinctive, its crescent-wrench c opened wide and every stroke drawn at a single thickness, with no swell anywhere. Arvo, a text serif, brings curves that refuse to close.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-belgrano: Baumans is all signage-like plainness, each line the same weight. Belgrano answers with open-mouthed serif curves that stay clear, and that traditional warmth is what makes the two worth putting together.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-biorhyme: Baumans draws spaghetti-like strokes of one width, with a wrench-shaped c that sounds commanding and distinctive. BioRhyme, a text serif, has brush-lifted curve ends and widely spaced capitals, so shrinking the heading would lose that edge.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-biorhyme-expanded: Baumans carries a distinctive crescent-wrench c, and its strokes never taper where they meet or end. And BioRhyme Expanded, a serif, leaves open gaps that split each word into single, bookish letters.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-biz-udmincho: Traditional in feeling, BIZ UDMincho is the quieter half here, its serif letters ending in a shallow curl with a wide gap. Baumans is the loud one, a plain unshaded line that never swells, so a slightly larger body size would help it hold its own.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-copse: Commanding is how Baumans reads, each stroke stout as a drawn pipe cleaner and its c opened like a wrench. Copse, a text serif, does the gentler job, letting daylight through every curved opening in literary, classic lines.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-cutive: Stout, wrench-mouthed letters with no thick or thin parts: that is Baumans. And Cutive, a classic serif, spreads out its running text with wide tracking and a generous opening in the c, which feels refined and literary.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-david-libre: Strip-cut and stubborn, Baumans has glyphs that look sliced from equal-width bands. But David Libre, a classic serif, lets its terminals hang open, which gives long lines a dignified, refined feel.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-enriqueta: A crescent-wrench c and a t whose crossbar and stem share one width make Baumans unmistakable. Enriqueta, a serif, sets chalk curves that stop well before closing, and that literary softness against the stout heading is the pair's best quality.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-fenix: Pencil-like lines that never thicken or thin define Baumans. Fenix, a classic serif, adds editorial curved strokes that end before they turn inward, giving the page a quieter second voice beneath that commanding heading.
